source.title: Data-driven progressive discovery of physical laws

hypothesis: A progressive chain improves held-out recovery only when intermediate structure is identifiable, under matched observations and search budgets.
alternatives: One-step symbolic regression matches or beats the chain under matched resources.
Apparent gain is caused by extra observations, compute, leakage or post-hoc chain selection.
Multiple structures are observationally equivalent and no unique mechanism is identified.
preregistration_requirements: Commit dataset generator, seed list, train/validation/test hashes and candidate grammar before execution.
Split by complete law family and parameter regime; do not use random rows alone.
Include noise, correlated distractors, dimensionally invalid candidates, a misspecified chain and an observational-equivalence negative control.
Freeze evaluation budgets and stop rules before opening the held-out set.
Retain all failed candidates, invalid proposals and seeds.
acceptance: Accept only a preregistered held-out or identifiable-structure improvement over the strongest baseline under matched budgets without worse constraint violations; ties and ambiguity are valid null outcomes.
stop_conditions: Unequal observations or unaccounted search budget
Candidate family violates declared dimensional or domain constraints
Apparent win only on training fit
Identifiability control incorrectly forces a unique mechanism
